column6: Worked: grad (x,10y), step 0.1 zeroes y and scales x by 0.9. Older text: Q1 explanation inequality is reversed (1/sqrt(C) < n/C iff C < n^2); Q2 calls Robbins-Monro conditions "necessary and sufficient" (they are sufficient); Explainer says SVRG/SAGA give O(1/T) (they give linear rates on strongly convex finite sums).
Bullet 2 overstated: in the interpolation regime (all per-example gradients vanish at the minimizer) fixed-step SGD does converge exactly. Added that qualifier.

Older text: Q4 keys "higher learning rate" as NOT implicit regularization, but large learning rates are widely studied as implicit regularizers; Q2 "random search" answer is weak; Explainer "nearly every direction of gradient descent encounters solutions that generalize" overstates.
Bullets 1 and 4 correctly temper the older Core Idea/Explainer claims about NTK and guaranteed generalization.
Worked: (ln1000+ln100)/0.05 = 230.3 -> 231; tenfold delta adds ln10/0.05 = 46.1.
Older text: Q4 (exponential time means not PAC-learnable, answer false) depends on the definition; many texts define PAC learnability statistically and call the time-bounded version "efficient".
Worked all 8 sign vectors: four give 1, four give 1/3; mean 2/3.

Older text: Q3 (empirical Rademacher complexity "always decreases" with n, answer true) is wrong as stated: it is sample-specific, a single-function class stays at 0, and only the expected version is non-increasing.
Worked with the file's (K+lambda I)^-1 convention: 0.01/0.001 = 10; 0.01/0.011 = 0.909. Older text: Q3 Landweber filter omits the step size eta.
Worked: phi(1) = (1, sqrt2, 1), norm^2 4; projection of (0,0,1) is phi(1)/4 = (1+x)^2/4; value 1, norm^2 1/4.

Older text: Q1 keyed option says "About 20,000" while its own arithmetic gives about 9,500. Core Idea and Explainer call the realizable rate with log(1/eps) "Theta"/"tight"; Hanneke (2016) showed the optimal rate is Theta((d + log(1/delta))/eps) with no log(1/eps) factor.

Bullet 4 absolute: zero-shot use of self-supervised models needs no labels. Changed to "usually still needs some labeled data". Older text: Q4 is a "what is the difference" question typed true-false with answer true (broken). Core Idea calls GPT masked-token prediction (it is next-token). Explainer lists BYOL as contrastive "with fewer negatives" (BYOL uses none).
Older text: Q3 (unlimited data means always the most complex class, answer true) fails on ties in approximation error and for infinite hierarchies.
Older text: Q4 is a "why" question typed true-false (broken). Explainer says permutation equivariance "ensures the model leverages sequential structure" (the opposite is true).

Bullet 2 dropped the mean-zero assumption (unit variance of q.k/sqrt(d) needs zero-mean entries). Bullet 4 said memory always grows with T^2; blockwise exact kernels such as FlashAttention avoid storing the full matrix. Qualified both.
Older text: Q2 keyed option says about 4,000 while its explanation computes 5,200.

Five-point rectangle step assumed four distinct extreme points ("the fifth point"). Extremes can coincide, so reworded: pick one point per extreme (at most four), and any left-over point lies in their bounding box.

Bullet 2 is correct. It contradicts older Q5, whose key ("Exactly 10" after failing on SOME 11-point set) is wrong: that gives only VC >= 10. Q5 left unedited as out of scope; it needs a fix. Older text also: Q1 keyed option and explanation give different rates.
Worked thresholds (+,- on x1<x2 fails), XOR diagonal, interior point.
Precision only, not counted: bullet 4 said VC dimension "counts the labelings"; the growth function counts them. Reworded to "depends on the labelings".
